gaps.concept: The perineal body anchors pelvic floor muscles; childbirth injury weakens support of the vagina and anal canal.
gaps.why_tested: A postpartum patient develops prolapse or incontinence after a midline perineal injury.

gaps.concept: Second-degree perineal tears involve perineal muscles; third-degree tears involve the anal sphincter; fourth-degree tears reach rectal mucosa.
gaps.why_tested: A delivery vignette asks which structures are injured at a stated tear depth.

gaps.concept: Puborectalis maintains the anorectal angle; relaxation straightens it during defecation.
gaps.why_tested: A stem asks how pelvic floor injury causes fecal incontinence.

gaps.concept: The pudendal nerve (S2–S4) passes around the ischial spine, enters the lesser sciatic foramen, and travels in Alcock canal.
gaps.why_tested: A labor analgesia or pelvic trauma vignette asks for the nerve or block landmark.

gaps.concept: Anterior vaginal wall weakness causes cystocele; posterior wall weakness causes rectocele; apical support failure causes uterine prolapse.
gaps.why_tested: A pelvic examination describes the location of a vaginal bulge.

gaps.concept: Obturator internus forms the lateral pelvic wall and its fascia forms Alcock canal; it is not part of the pelvic diaphragm.
gaps.why_tested: An anatomy image asks whether a labeled muscle forms the pelvic wall or floor.

gaps.concept: Pelvic parasympathetics contract the detrusor and relax the bladder outlet; sympathetics relax the detrusor and contract the bladder neck.
gaps.why_tested: A nerve injury vignette asks whether urine storage or voiding is impaired.

gaps.concept: The external urethral sphincter is voluntary and pudendal-innervated; the internal bladder-neck sphincter is smooth muscle under autonomic control.
gaps.why_tested: A pelvic nerve lesion or urinary continence stem asks which sphincter is affected.

gaps.concept: Pelvic parasympathetics mediate erection; sympathetics mediate seminal emission and bladder-neck closure; pudendal motor fibers mediate ejaculatory expulsion.
gaps.why_tested: A prostate surgery vignette distinguishes erectile dysfunction, impaired emission, and retrograde ejaculation.

gaps.concept: First-stage labor pain refers to T10–L1; second-stage vaginal and perineal pain travels mainly through pudendal fibers to S2–S4.
gaps.why_tested: A labor analgesia stem asks which neural pathway carries pain at a given stage.

gaps.concept: Ovarian and testicular lymph drains to para-aortic nodes, unlike scrotal skin, which drains to superficial inguinal nodes.
gaps.why_tested: A gonadal tumor vignette asks for the first nodal basin.

gaps.concept: Uterine fundus lymph can reach para-aortic nodes or follow the round ligament to superficial inguinal nodes; cervix drains to pelvic nodes.
gaps.why_tested: A uterine or cervical lesion stem asks which lymph nodes may be involved.

gaps.concept: Upper vaginal lymph drains chiefly to pelvic iliac nodes; lower vaginal lymph drains to superficial inguinal nodes.
gaps.why_tested: A vaginal lesion stem identifies its level and asks for nodal spread.

gaps.concept: The valveless prostatic venous plexus communicates with vertebral veins, permitting prostate cancer spread to the spine.
gaps.why_tested: A patient with prostate cancer develops vertebral metastases.

gaps.concept: Prostate cancer usually arises in the peripheral zone, palpable posteriorly; benign prostatic hyperplasia arises in the periurethral transition zone.
gaps.why_tested: A stem contrasts a hard posterior nodule with urinary obstruction from gland enlargement.

gaps.concept: The uterine tube comprises fimbriae, infundibulum, ampulla, and isthmus; fertilization usually occurs in the ampulla.
gaps.why_tested: An anatomy or infertility stem asks where fertilization occurs.

gaps.concept: The ampulla is the most common tubal ectopic implantation site; tubal scarring impairs embryo transport and raises ectopic risk.
gaps.why_tested: A patient with prior pelvic infection has pain, bleeding, and no intrauterine pregnancy.

gaps.concept: The open fimbrial end connects the female reproductive tract to the peritoneal cavity, allowing ascending infection to cause pelvic peritonitis.
gaps.why_tested: A pelvic inflammatory disease stem asks how infection reaches the peritoneum.

gaps.concept: The ectocervix has stratified squamous epithelium; the endocervix has columnar epithelium; their transformation zone is vulnerable to dysplasia.
gaps.why_tested: A cervical sampling or histology stem asks where dysplasia develops.

gaps.concept: Paramesonephric ducts form the uterine tubes, uterus, cervix, and upper vagina; the lower vagina develops with the urogenital sinus.
gaps.why_tested: A congenital vaginal or uterine anomaly asks for its embryologic source.

gaps.concept: Failed Müllerian duct fusion causes a bicornuate uterus; failed septum resorption causes a septate uterus; duct agenesis causes MRKH syndrome.
gaps.why_tested: An imaging or primary amenorrhea vignette asks which developmental step failed.

gaps.concept: Mesonephric ducts form the epididymis, ductus deferens, seminal vesicles, and ejaculatory ducts under testosterone influence.
gaps.why_tested: A sexual-development vignette asks which internal male structures depend on Wolffian ducts.

gaps.concept: The prostate develops from endodermal buds of the urogenital sinus.
gaps.why_tested: An embryology stem asks for the tissue origin of a male pelvic gland.

gaps.concept: In males, the ductus deferens crosses superior to the ureter near the posterior bladder.
gaps.why_tested: A male pelvic surgery image asks which duct crosses the ureter.

gaps.concept: The bladder trigone lies between the ureteric orifices and internal urethral orifice; oblique ureter entry helps prevent reflux.
gaps.why_tested: A bladder diagram or vesicoureteral reflux stem asks for the relevant anatomy.

gaps.concept: Superior vesical arteries arise from the patent proximal umbilical artery; inferior vesical and middle rectal arteries supply male pelvic viscera.
gaps.why_tested: An internal iliac artery diagram asks which branch supplies a labeled pelvic organ.

gaps.concept: Pelvic fracture can rupture the membranous urethra, causing blood at the meatus and urinary extravasation.
gaps.why_tested: A trauma vignette asks which urethral segment was injured.

gaps.concept: The superior rectal artery arises from the inferior mesenteric artery; middle rectal from internal iliac; inferior rectal from internal pudendal.
gaps.why_tested: A rectal surgery or angiography stem asks for arterial origin at a specified level.

gaps.concept: Superior rectal veins drain to the portal system; middle and inferior rectal veins drain systemically, forming a portosystemic anastomosis.
gaps.why_tested: A portal hypertension stem asks where venous blood can bypass the liver.
